chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Bakkar ibn Kardam, from Mufazzal ibn Umar and Abd al-Mu'min al-Ansari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Allah (Mighty and Majestic) said: I am Allah. There is no god except Me. I am the Creator of good and evil. So beatitude is for the one upon whose hands I cause good to flow, and woe is for the one upon whose hands I cause evil to flow, and woe is for the one who says: How is that so, and how is this so?
Yunus said: It means the one who denies this matter through his understanding of it.

key_terms.أَجْرَيْتُ: Literally 'I caused to flow' — a metaphor for God directing events through human agency without compelling the will.
key_terms.بِتَفَقُّهٍ: Through understanding/tafaqquh — Yunus's gloss indicates the condemnation is for intellectual denial masquerading as religious inquiry.
key_terms.خَالِقُ الْخَيْرِ وَالشَّرِّ: Creator of good and evil — affirming divine omnipotence and absolute sovereignty over all creation, foundational to Shia theology on divine decree (qada and qadar).
key_terms.طُوبَى: Beatitude/blessedness — an expression of supreme felicity, related to the word 'goodness' (tuba). Also a reference to a tree in Paradise.
key_terms.وَيْلٌ: Woe — an expression of condemnation, misery, or destruction; used in the Quran for those in hellfire.

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith from al-Kafi say about God being the Creator of good and evil?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a Divine (hadith qudsi) statement relayed by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), affirming absolute Divine sovereignty over both good and evil in the world. God declares Himself the Creator of all that occurs — both good and evil — granting blessedness to those whose hands become instruments of good, while warning of woe for those through whom evil flows, and condemning those who question the wisdom of divine decree. Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman adds an important gloss: the final warning is directed at those who deny divine decree while pretending to engage with it intellectually.
word_analysis: I have caused to flow/I flow
